nyc_found: For the 2025–26 school year, NYCDOE reported 793,300 students enrolled in K-12 grades.
match_found: The data shows a total of 870,793 pre-K-12th grade students enrolled in Colorado schools, a decrease of 1.2% compared to fall 2024.
finding: Both numbers verify exactly and both are current (2025-26 counts). The City Journal source calls the NYC figure "K-12 grades" without explicitly saying "district schools," but cross-checking against NYC Charter School Center's own 2025-26 claim (charters are 15.2% of ~990,000 total NYC public K-12 students, implying district-only enrollment near 840,000) leaves some unreconciled gap with 793,300 -- the two sources aren't perfectly consistent, though both point to district-only being well under Colorado's total. The caveat correctly discloses that adding charter and pre-K enrollment would flip the comparison.

nyc_found: As of April 2026, the City employed 291,717 active full-time workers, largely unchanged from March and down from 292,483 at the start of the Mamdani Administration in January.
match_found: Texas row in Census govsemp API, GOVTYPE 002 (state government): ["Texas","EP0005","002","2025","301402","2025","48"] -- 301,402 full-time state government employees for 2025.
finding: Both figures verify exactly against their sources. The caveat discloses that the Census survey reflects a March 2025 payroll, but doesn't spell out that the NYC figure is 13 months newer (April 2026) -- a wider gap than the caveat's wording implies. nyc_found: NYCHA serves 298,206 authorized residents ... through the conventional public housing program (Section 9) ... NYCHA also serves 46,455 authorized residents ... within 92 developments that have been converted under the Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT)/Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) programs.
conflict: A newer, equally official NYCHA source -- the city's Preliminary Mayor's Management Report for FY2026 (nyc.gov/assets/operations/downloads/pdf/pmmr2026/nycha.pdf) -- gives different, lower figures: "NYCHA serves 285,055 authorized residents ... through the conventional public housing program (Section 9) and 51,904 authorized residents ... within 108 developments that were converted to the Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT) program." That sums to 336,959, about 2.2% below the 344,661 used in the claim.
finding: The 298,206 + 46,455 = 344,661 figure matches the cited NYCHA Fact Sheet exactly, but that fact sheet is dated January 2025 (20 months old). A newer NYCHA count published in February 2026 gives 336,959, a meaningfully different total. Both figures still put NYC well below Cleveland's 363,608, so the comparison direction holds either way, but the specific number used is stale and a more current one exists.

nyc_found: More than 100 higher education institutions host a student population of over 503,000.
match_found: NCES Digest Table 304.10 (2023 edition), Massachusetts, 2022: 468,960 -- the most recent year shown in that table.
finding: Both numbers verify exactly. The Massachusetts figure is genuinely stale (fall 2022, now roughly four years old) and NCES appears to have stopped publishing per-state breakdowns in this specific table series since the 2022 data year, so this is the most current version available -- the caveat is accurate. The NYCEDC report's footnotes don't specify which year's federal enrollment data underlies its 503,000 figure, so the caveat's implication that NYC's count is more current ("a 2024 count") could not be independently verified from the source itself.

nyc_found: NYCPS employs over 77,000 teachers in over 1,800 district schools in 32 school districts.
match_found: The total number of teachers has risen by over 8,258 since 2018, from 65,815 to 74,073. ... B.5 Total number of teachers ... 2022: 74,073.
conflict: NYC's own more current data undercuts the caveat's prediction. The city's Preliminary Mayor's Management Report for FY2026 (nyc.gov/assets/operations/downloads/pdf/pmmr2026/doe.pdf) shows NYCPS teacher headcount rising to 81,249 as of the first four months of Fiscal 2026 (around October 2025), up from 77,585 in FY25 -- a gain of roughly 3,700 in about four months. Separately, Ireland's own newer data (Statistical Bulletin, August 2024, and reporting citing 2023/24 Department of Education figures) shows Irish teacher numbers around 79,000-79,390 for the 2023/24 school year.
finding: The cited 77,000/74,073 figures are accurate for what they were current as of (NYC's MMR2025 report and Ireland's 2022 indicators), but the caveat's claim that "Ireland has probably passed New York City since" is not well supported once NYC's own newer numbers are checked -- NYCPS's headcount also grew substantially (to roughly 81,249 by late 2025), likely still ahead of Ireland's most recent count near 79,000-79,390. The caveat assumes only Ireland is growing while treating NYC's count as fixed at "over 77,000," which is the misleading part.
